chunks: And Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār narrated:
That one of our companions wrote, by the hand of Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq, to ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: "Should I give a man from my brothers two or three dirhams from zakat?"
So he wrote: "Do so, if Allah wills."

key_terms.إِخْوَانِي: my brothers, meaning fellow believers or companions in faith
key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ: three dirhams, indicating another small amount under discussion
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمَيْنِ: two dirhams, a small monetary amount
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat (obligatory alms-tax) from which the payment is being given
key_terms.اِفْعَلْ: do it; an expression of permission from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.كَتَبَ: wrote, indicating a written question and written reply

ai.seo_question: Can a person give two or three dirhams from zakat to one of his believing brothers?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal question about giving a small amount of zakat to one of the believer's brothers. The Imam عليه السلام replies with permission, indicating the permissibility of giving two or three dirhams from zakat in such a case.
